records.region: Retamilla–Tilihuiche–Tana drainage and Pisagua Viejo coastal setting, Región de Tarapacá, northern Chile.
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded middle and lower component name; not a completed representative identity for the entire modeled object.
records.material_pending_reason: Neither inspected hydrographic publication supplies the complete chosen southward connection from the eastern unnamed opening, through the intervening isolated drainage, to the westward Retamilla headward corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected upper route is the southern Retamilla-side approach, rather than the separate northern Camiña course. Camiña/Tana source narratives cannot replace the actual chosen eastern opening.
records.completion_scope: The opening, all fifteen stored parts, their joins and the actual coastal ending were considered against acquired original map views. Long middle and lower portions correspond at ordinary corridor scale; the headward through-link remains a substantive evidence gap. This is not a completed whole-system or name-scope-hold result.
records.supported_name_scope: The long selected Retamilla corridor upstream of its lower convergence with the Tilihuiche and Tana approaches. The unproved upper transfer and distinct coastal receiving reach are excluded from the name's established scope.

component_scope_limits: Quebrada de Retamilla is a supported selected component, not a uniform name for the entire model.

Tilihuiche is the map spelling for a separate joining course; Tiliviche is the coastal assessment's spelling and downstream naming account. No exact legal synonym or transition boundary is adjudicated.
The separate northern Camiña/Tana headwaters are not selected.
No lake, reservoir, glacier or engineered conduit was established as a selected passage. None is invented to bridge the upper gap.

The coastal assessment describes regional summer runoff and tributaries with little or no flow. Source-drawn channels do not establish perennial water or continuous present hydraulic passage through arid terrain.

records.region: Lima and Huarochirí, Peru; upper Río Blanco–Yuracmayo corridor through the Rímac valley to the Pacific north of Callao.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative downstream river-system identity for the selected Río Blanco–Yuracmayo–Rímac route. It is not asserted as the scalar name of the upper arm, reservoir and every selected reach.
records.completion_scope: The independent INGEMMET original covers the entire selected corridor, including the eastern headwater arm, Yuracmayo and its outlet, Río Blanco into the Chicla-side junction, Rímac/San Mateo past Matucana and Surco, Santa Eulalia confluence, Lima and the actual Pacific outlet. All 33 parts are accounted for. Distinct reach names and regulated storage do not prevent this bounded representative identity. The unavailable ANA study is not needed to fill a remaining source gap.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative downstream river-system identity for the selected Río Blanco–Yuracmayo–Rímac route. It is not asserted as the scalar name of the upper arm, reservoir and every selected reach.

scope_limits: The independent map supports the chosen upper arm but does not supply an unambiguous individual name for that entire arm; it is not labeled Río Rímac by this finding.
The report uses Río Rímac and San Mateo for different descriptions of the upper main valley. No precise name-transition point or formal registry match is asserted.
Yuracmayo is regulated storage on the selected route. This finding establishes the mapped passage, not contemporary release quantities or diversion operations.
The exact modern coast, banks and small urban side-channel configuration are not resolved at1:500,000. The mapped main corridor and ocean endpoint are established.

records.region: Southwestern Buenos Aires province, Argentina; Ventania headwater–Los Chilenos–Chasicó basin setting.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported receiving-trunk name and bounded system candidate; incomplete representative correspondence.
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen opening and upper feeder joins, selected Los Chilenos entry/traverse/exit, and complete substantial middle through-route lack sufficiently discriminating original cartography. The terminal lagoon is established, but a generalized basin diagram and regional prose cannot close these selected-route gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected endpoint is inland in the Chasicó lake setting. No Atlantic outlet, unrelated Sauce Chico corridor, or tributary name inferred from basin membership is substituted for it.
records.completion_scope: All selected parts and their joins were considered at ordinary regional scale. Only the terminal-lake component has complete correspondence; upper and middle material gaps remain. A natural seasonal lake link is documented, but its exact selected traversal is not established. No managed connector or current flow state is asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: The named trunk between Laguna Los Chilenos and Laguna Chasicó, with the receiving-lake setting established. The chosen upper feeder and all intervening selected connections are not established.

scope_limits: The selected headwater cannot be given a local name from the acquired materials.
Upper and middle source-to-selection correspondence remains incomplete even though a recognized connected basin exists.
The lake-entry and inland-terminal interpretation is regional; exact shoreline, bank, hydraulic state and current operations were not investigated.
Formal registry status is unverified. Different river, feeder and lake names may legitimately coexist in one representative system.

records.region: Victoria Island, Arctic Canada: eastern inland lakes, Kagloryuak River corridor and the eastern head of Prince Albert Sound.
records.material_pending_reason: The source depicts a named northern Kagloryuak valley and separate southern tributaries and lake chains. It does not unambiguously establish the selected southern transfer and its complete rejoining sequence, especially constituent sublines20–27. The gap concerns the selected connected route at ordinary corridor scale, not an exact bank, vertex or modern-channel requirement.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins in small lake-and-stream country west of a large unnamed lake, bends northeast and east into that lake, follows its southern lake-and-channel outlet and the southwestward river into the labeled Kagloryuak corridor. In the lower inland section the selection makes a southern excursion through lake and tributary country, while the labeled river valley continues farther north. The historical map does not securely establish the selected transfer across that interval. The final lower river and its entry to the eastern Prince Albert Sound water are identifiable independently of the geometry's sea classification.
records.completion_scope: The successful original covers the whole selected extent, and all32 constituent sublines were considered. Original source-only windows were read for the opening, lake inlet/passage/outlet, eastern descent, middle river, southern lower-country transfer, lower joins and actual terminal. Coverage of an area by map pixels does not establish the selected through-link: the southern interval remains a substantive correspondence gap. This is one source-material-pending record, not a completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: The original labels Kagloryuak River along the substantial westward middle/lower river. The named corridor and its Prince Albert Sound outlet are supported. The name is not accepted for the entire selected path because the selected southern lower-course lake/tributary transfer is not established continuously.

scope_limits: Kagloryuak River is supported by its map label on the river, not by the publication title alone.
Unnamed lake passages retain lake roles; no river name is forced onto every lake or feeder.
The unresolved selected southern through-link prevents a completed representative-system identity.
The historical map's lack of a particular local name is not proof that no current local or official name exists.
No current flow permanence, exact modern banks, formal naming boundary or surveyed length is established.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
